scope: Design observation only; no candidate is user-accepted by this file.

observations.observation: Open thorax, bilateral pelvis, limb rails, palm and foot regions form the strongest human silhouette.
Every Core segment has exact endpoints and a consistent octahedral direction.
Square octahedral sections and warm roll marks expose orientation most directly.
Small bright joint centers remain clean against the low primitive count.
Head cube plus independent gaze target creates the clearest static facing intent.
Open rib bands communicate upper-body volume without a closed torso shell.
Bilateral arcs, transverse ring and center bridge expose load transfer.
Clavicle arcs and scapula plates distinguish shoulder movement regions.
Waisted upper arm and dual forearm rails provide human-readable segmentation.
Waisted thigh, paired lower-leg rails and structured foot give the clearest leg chain.
Palm plate and digit direction hints communicate hand extent without labels.
Heel, arch, forefoot and toe direction are visible as separate cues.
Magenta rings, boxes, squares and diamonds are distinct from cyan bones.
Hand/foot outlines and pole diamonds provide a direct static vocabulary for a future editor.
Shoulder, dual forearm and palm regions make the gesture path easiest to inspect.
Pelvis bridge and detailed lower limbs make compression and extension regions easiest to inspect.
Open thorax, shoulder girdle and palms make load-bearing posture easiest to reason about.
The primitive count and overlay density are lowest.
All candidates use the identical frozen 20-joint, 19-segment Reference T snapshot and projector.
The contact sheet is evidence for selection; this study deliberately does not choose or accept a winner.
